text:
An approval screen should earn confidence, not carry it alone.

CERT-In reports an AI-assisted campaign targeting Indian financial entities through their payment interfaces. Its earlier advisory describes direct payment calls using stolen credentials to bypass application checks.

My concern is the gap between a decision someone approves and the instruction that actually moves money. A reassuring screen shows one part of that journey. I would want evidence that the final transfer remains bound to the approved payment.

That matters because the people entrusted with approving payments need their decisions to govern what happens next. Otherwise, their responsibility may extend further than their control.

For business and IT leaders, I would start with one payment: trace its approval all the way to transfer. Ask the team to demonstrate what stops a different recipient or amount from being accepted at that final step.

The leadership task is to make approval meaningful where it matters most: where money leaves.
